To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of Ce3+ ion-based filters in the form of a cooling and filtering solution in the flashlamp enclosure and in a monolithic laser enclosure made of quartz, in combination with flashlamps enclosed by quartz bulbs, is a promising method for increasing the efficiency of neodymium YAG and YAP lasers.

in neodymium lasers with ultraviolet Ce3+ -based filters the maximum efficiency of the flashlamp, the laser enclosure, and the cooling liquid is 3.2 ± 0.3% in the case of free-running YAG lasers and 3.8% in the case for free-running YAL lasers.

ultraviolet filters based upon Ce3+ ions are effective in the case of Nd:YAG and Nd:YAL lasers, and the most effective is a monolithic enclosure, made of KU1 quartz, and flashlamps, enclosed in KU1 or KLB4 quartz bulbs, with a cooling and a filtering liquid in the shape of an aqueous answer of CeCl3, with at least 0,1 mol/liter concentration of Ce3+ ions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of ultraviolet Ce-based filters in the design of laser illumination enclosures and cooling and filtering liquids.
the use of Ce3+-based ultraviolet filters to increase the efficiency of laser illumination enclosures and to reduce the level of ultraviolet radiation.
the development of a method for improving the efficiency of neodymium lasers by using Ce3+ ions as filters in the flashlamps and in the cooling and filtering liquids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of ultraviolet Ce-based filters in the components of neodymium laser illumination enclosures is a promising way to improve the efficiency of neodymium lasers.

the use of the Ce3+-based ultraviolet filter is a highly effective method of increasing the efficiency of the neodymium laser illumination enclosure and of increasing the overall efficiency of the laser.

the most efficient is the use of a flashlamp enclosed in a KU-1 bulb, a cooling and filtering solution in the form of a CeCl3 aqueous solution with the Ce3 + ion concentration of at most 0.1 M, and a monolithic enclosure also made of KU1 quartz.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of ultraviolet filters in the components of the laser system increases the efficiency by a factor of 3-5.
the use of ultraviolet Ce-3+ ion-based filters in the components of laser illumination enclosures is an effective method of increasing their dynamic efficiency.
the use of ultraviolet filters in neodymium-dope YAG and YAG lasers is effective.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of Ce3+-based ultraviolet filters in neodymium lasers is a promising approach to increasing their dynamic efficiency.
the use of Ce3+ ion-containing filters makes it possible to increase the efficiency of the laser illumination enclosure by a factor of at least 1.5.
it is possible to increase the efficiency of neodymium lasers by using CeCl3 aqueous solution as a cooling liquid and by using Ce3+-doped KU-1 filters.
